dossiers.thesis_summary: Binary on the ARCHER II (NCT06510816, n=659) Month 15 topline for vonaprument in geographic atrophy. The primary endpoint is protection against a confirmed BCVA loss of 15 letters or more, which would make it the first vision-preserving GA drug. The company reconfirmed Q4 2026 timing in its 12-Aug Q2 release and again on 24-Sep (Retina Society PR). No data release or new offering had appeared as of 30-Sep. Win leg is about $11.00/sh (vision-preserving GA asset, with Iveric/Astellas $5.9B Apr-2023 as the pre-approval comp, net of ATM dilution). Lose leg is about $1.70/sh (cash at readout plus a haircut value for tanruprubart in GBS, which has no BLA filed yet, plus platform residual). Spot is $4.13.
dossiers.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that ARCHER II replicates the Phase 2 ARCHER vision-protection signal at Month 15. The refutation case is that the Phase 2 BCVA benefit was not the primary lesion-growth endpoint, so it may be a small-sample finding. Also, on 12-Aug-2026 the sponsor added a Month 24 dual primary endpoint while still blinded, before the M15 readout. That can be read as a hedge against a marginal M15 result. A miss at M15 could then leave the stock in a limbo where M24 is still alive (Q3-2027), not a clean floor print. Separately, ATM use (about $118M of capacity) and possible draws on the Oxford facility could lower per-share capture in both legs.

dossiers.thesis_summary: Aquarian has signed to buy Brighthouse for $70.00 a share in cash. Shareholders approved on 12 Feb 2026. Closing now depends only on insurance regulators in Delaware (the Form A change-of-control review), New York and Massachusetts. The deal missed the original 6 Sep 2026 outside date and was automatically extended to 6 Dec 2026. At $52.00 the stock is about 35% below the offer, which prices in roughly a 1-in-3 chance of closing. The reason is real doubt about the deal: Delaware is questioning where Aquarian's capital comes from (about $3B of it is backstopped by Mubadala), and no Form A hearing has been noticed. If the deal closes, the stock goes to $70. If it breaks, the stock falls back to a standalone value of about $43. There is some unpriced upside if it breaks: Talcott/Sixth Street has sent a non-binding letter saying it is still interested.
dossiers.kill_risk: The most load-bearing claim is that the deal closes at $70. The live record weakens it. Delaware is actively examining Aquarian's funding: Bloomberg and AdvisorHub reported on 10 Sep 2026 that the founder was questioned in a closed-door meeting. As of about 29 Sep there is still no Form A hearing notice, and New York and Massachusetts must also approve. Delaware still has to notice a hearing, hold it, and issue a final order, and 68 days is tight for that. So 6 Dec looks more like the date either side can walk away than a likely closing date, and a second extension (by mutual consent) into 2027 is probable. Sixth Street/Talcott's renewed interest (Bloomberg, 22 Sep) gives Brighthouse's board an easy alternative if it wants to terminate. On a break, the $225.5M parent fee is unlikely to be paid if the break comes from regulators or burdensome conditions. The downside also has a tail below $43: the banker's low standalone value of about $30, and AM Best still has the ratings under review with negative implications.

dossiers.thesis_summary: Dingdong agreed on 5 Feb 2026 to sell its China business to Meituan (Two Hearts Investments) for US$717m, with no financing contingency. Shareholders approved it on 27 Mar 2026. The one remaining regulatory gate is SAMR anti-monopoly clearance, which has not come, and the proceeds are then returned to holders. As of 30 Sep 2026 the deal is still pending: the newest EDGAR filing is a director's Form 3 on 16 Sep, the last 6-K is the 21 Aug Q2 release saying the deal awaits SAMR, and there is no press report of clearance, conditions, withdrawal or repricing. The stock trades at $2.18 against a verified US$267.1m of cash held outside the sale perimeter (about $1.13 per ADS), which puts a floor under the break case. The event-win value is about $3.20 per ADS on 236.2m ADS after a leakage reserve and non-controlling interests (NCI). The break value is about $1.65. That is roughly 1.9:1, not the ~2.56:1 the board shows.
dossiers.kill_risk: SAMR clearance never comes, or comes with conditions Meituan will not accept, before the ~5 Feb 2027 end date (which can be extended). If the SPA lapses without a refusal, no fee is paid. If Dingdong fails a controllable condition (overseas carve-out, non-resident indirect-transfer tax filing), Dingdong itself owes the US$75m fee (about -$0.32/ADS). The stock then reprices to a China-ADR stub near the $1.65 52-week low, or toward $1.13 of cash in a hard tail. A second leg: net-cash and working-capital price adjustments plus leakage after the US$280m sweep could shave the US$717m. I reserved US$25m for this, but the size is not disclosed.

dossiers.thesis_summary: FDA decision on the MOLBREEVI (inhaled molgramostim) BLA for autoimmune PAP is due by 22 Nov 2026 under Priority Review. The date was set by the 15 Apr 2026 major amendment (moved from 22 Aug), which cited no safety, efficacy or CMC concerns, and the 11 Aug Q2 release repeated it. The last company release was 24 Aug (ERS encore data). Nothing has fired or slipped as of 30 Sep. Phase 3 IMPALA-2 was positive, and the drug has Breakthrough and Fast Track designations. The binary is approval (~$8, rerating to a commercial-stage orphan launch) or CRL (~$2.5). UK MHRA (Q4 2026) and EMA (Q1 2027) decisions come after it.
dossiers.kill_risk: Load-bearing claim: the 22 Nov date is a clean approval shot. Refutation attempt: the BLA was refused on manufacturing (CMC) grounds in May 2025, and in Apr 2026 FDA information requests were large enough to count as a major amendment. No public source confirms that the pre-license inspection of the third-party GM-CSF drug-substance and device site has passed. CMC-driven CRLs at contract manufacturers have been common in 2025-26. A second CMC strike would also void both approval-gated financings (the $75M RTW royalty and the up-to-$75M Hercules tranche) at once, which would push dilution into a lower print. Residual risk is a CMC or inspection CRL, not efficacy.

dossiers.thesis_summary: The GFORCE-1 full readout for MRT-8102 is a Phase 1 trial of an oral NLRP3 molecular-glue degrader in people with high cardiovascular risk. It is real, unfired and specific to the company. Monte Rosa guides it only to "H2 2026" (Q2 release, 6 Aug 2026). Enrolment and dosing are complete. Interim data showed an 85% median CRP reduction at 4 weeks, so the result will turn more on the dose-response, how long the effect lasts and safety than on whether the drug works at all. Price is $11.74, about $992M market cap and about 84.5M shares. The $626M of cash at Q2 plus the $50M Novartis milestone for MRT-6160 (paid 8 Sep) comes to roughly $7/share. That leaves little more than $4/share of value on MRT-8102, the Novartis milestone stream and the platform. Re-marked axes: win $21, floor $8.50, p = 0.55.
dossiers.kill_risk: The thesis leans hardest on the claim that a clean full GFORCE-1 dataset re-rates the stock toward about $21. That is weak for three reasons. First, the headline efficacy (85% CRP cut) was already published in the interim, so a confirmatory full readout could be a sell-the-news event. Second, after the Jul-2026 ZEUS failure (HR 0.99, taken from the skeptic record and not re-verified here), investors may discount CRP-lowering as a surrogate for cardiovascular benefit. Third, the timing is a company-controlled window with no date. The Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley conferences in September passed without narrowing it, and the readout could slip into 2027 or come out quietly at a medical meeting. On the downside, cash of about $7/share limits the loss, but a safety signal (liver or infection) in the full dataset would push toward cash value.

director.memo: Shape: two new seats, SVRA and ANNX, which take the book to 9 unresolved seats at 50/9 = 5.56% each. Both beat the median held seat on fresh verdict-A debates with dated 2026 milestones. SVRA is a Priority Review PDUFA on 22-Nov with CMC-only residual risk, EV ~+30%. ANNX has the rare conviction-5 debate on the ARCHER II Month 15 readout in Q4, EV ~+31%. Both are binary_prob, so both use defined-risk calls: Feb-2027 for SVRA and Apr-2027 for ANNX. This overrides the CRO's 'equity only' notes because the binary gate is hard. ANNX has an explicit liquidity gate: if its chain never tightens, the seat stays unopened rather than being forced into an unfillable fill. Passed: DDL (a 2027 contractual end date against the fast-return horizon, which costs the book its only Deal-completion diversity), CAPR (the edge halved by an unexplained gap, and no tradeable defined-risk chain), and GLUE (an ordinary edge on a public-interim, sell-the-news staging readout). Concentration: the book is now 8 of 9 seats FDA/biotech (4 FDA_approval_decision, 3 FDA_clinical_readout, 1 FDA_pathway_feedback) plus FIG as the only Idiosyncratic seat. That is a heavy lean into one family. I accept it knowingly: the non-FDA survivors this run failed on merit or horizon, and the defined-risk structure on every binary is what bounds the downside. Diversifiers to seat first when a dossier appears: MGNI and CLVT. Carried watchlist: BBIO is re-championed (dated 27-Nov PDUFA, verdict A). CLVT, PVLA and MGNI stay de-prioritized and tracked. EYPT (catalyst fired as a miss), DBVT (2027 approval), GERN (2028 final analysis, undated interim) and a junk placeholder row were demoted to passed with reasons. Macro (ADVISORY, DISCIPLINE): cash-soon catalysts get paid in this phase. SVRA's approval unlocks $150M of non-dilutive financing plus launch revenue, which fits. ANNX re-rates a longer-duration asset and is exposed to ATM dilution, which cuts against the phase, but I seat it anyway on the dated evidence and a Q4 resolution. The regime context block is dated 2026-07 and is near its ~2026-10 staleness limit, so it was read cautiously: the warm biotech tape was treated as compressing entry edges, not as a reason to loosen. No caps exist, so none needed re-checking. The only real constraint was dilution, from 7.14% to 5.56% per seat.
